title: A Spire for the Choir
premise: Beatrix Quintana has spent her life mapping the unmapped from inside the Hollow Valley, the one place where magic cannot follow—and where she, a child of two realms, can exist at all. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark on the same night, Beatrix learns they are the living keystone of a covenant their parents helped break: a pact that kept the magical realms from devouring each other. Hunted by the Wardens of the extinguished sky and guided by a found family of exiles—a disgraced star-priest, a memory-eating fox spirit, and a Warden deserter—Beatrix must journey to the Spire of Accord and reforge the covenant with their own blood and memories as ink. In the end, Beatrix chooses to give up every memory of the valley to seal the new accord, keeping justice alive outside any law but losing the home that made them; their found family vows to become the memory they no longer have.
about_author: Ivo Hartwell is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of places that no longer exist. They write fantasy about borders—geographic, legal, and personal—from a drafty house full of orphaned atlases.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. While inking a map of a realm they've never seen, Beatrix watches the stars vanish one by one, then feels the valley's wards shatter like glass in their chest. The village elder demands answers Beatrix doesn't have. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in wonder—the first night the world has ever asked something of them.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, with a flashback to childhood. Searching their late mother's cartography chest, Beatrix finds a covenant fragment naming them as 'the keystone' and learns the valley wasn't hiding them—it was protecting the realms from them. A Warden patrol arrives asking for 'the Quintana child.' Emotional beat: the floor of identity giving way.

chapters.title: Three Exiles and a Fox
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Fleeing through the broken ward-line, Beatrix collides with Sera Voss, a defrocked star-priest, and Dain, a Warden deserter—and is promptly robbed by Wick, a fox spirit who eats memories instead of food. Reluctantly, four strangers bind into a traveling company. Emotional beat: wary, funny first sparks of found family.

chapters.title: The Road of Unmapped Things
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The company crosses a landscape rewriting itself now that the covenant is failing: rivers running uphill, towns remembering different histories each dawn. Beatrix's maps are the only thing holding geography steady, revealing their power—and painting a target on them. Emotional beat: awe curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: Wick Remembers Too Much
chapters.summary: Wick's POV. The fox spirit confesses it once ate a memory belonging to Beatrix's mother—the true terms of the old covenant—and offers to give it back, though returning it may kill Beatrix. Dain argues against; Sera argues for truth. Emotional beat: grief and tenderness, the cost of knowing.

chapters.title: The Warden's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Captured by Wardens, Dain bargains using his old rank while Beatrix discovers the Wardens aren't villains but bookkeepers of a dead law, executing 'irregularities' like Beatrix out of rote duty. The company escapes when Dain burns his own service ledger. Emotional beat: rage at lawful injustice, loyalty cemented in fire.

chapters.title: Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The long winter arrives early, freezing magic mid-shape and trapping refugees between warring realms. Beatrix uses their blood-keystone nature to hold a pass open, nearly dying, and admits aloud they'd rather break than let people freeze for their sake. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered freely, love made undeniable.

chapters.title: The Spire of Accord
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The company reaches the Spire, where the ghosts of the original covenant-makers—including Beatrix's mother—demand payment in memory. Wick volunteers to carry what Beatrix must surrender so nothing is truly lost. Emotional beat: solemnity, the weight of inheritance finally accepted.

chapters.title: A Covenant Reforged
chapters.summary: Climax, rotating POV across all four. As the Wardens assault the Spire to erase the keystone permanently, Beatrix writes the new covenant in their own remembered life—every mapped line, every valley morning—while Sera relights the stars, Dain holds the stair, and Wick guards the surrendered memories. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: The Map Without a Name
chapters.summary: Wick's POV. The covenant holds; the realms breathe again. Beatrix wakes with no past, holding a blank map, among three friends who promise to tell them everything—one story at a time. The final image: Beatrix begins drawing the first new line, labeled simply 'home.' Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal; memory lives on in those who love you.
